name: Switch
description: An on/off control for a setting that takes effect as soon as it is flipped, such as email notifications. If the choice is only applied when a form is submitted, use a Checkbox.

elements.name: Label
elements.description: Names the setting; stays the same when on or off

elements.name: Track
elements.description: Background that shows the on or off state

elements.name: Thumb
elements.description: Knob that sits at the start when off and the end when on

elements.name: Description
elements.description: Hint under the label, linked with aria-describedby

variants.caption: Label before — settings list, off and on
Label after — switch first, then label
Description — hint text under the label
variants.htmlOutline: A weekly summary of activity.

variants.caption: State text — On or Off beside the track
variants.htmlOutline: On

usageNotes: Use a Switch for a setting that applies the moment it's flipped. In a form that is saved with a submit button, use a Checkbox.
Add role="switch" to a native checkbox so screen readers announce on and off instead of checked. The checkbox still handles focus, Space and form submission.
Label the setting, not the action: "Email notifications", not "Turn on email notifications". The label must not change between states.
Don't show the state by color alone (WCAG 1.4.1). The thumb position carries it, and the track and thumb need 3:1 contrast against their surroundings (WCAG 1.4.11).
For a button that stays pressed, such as Bold in an editor, use a Toggle button.
